findings.summary: The Windows acceptance command cannot exercise the work-branch build.
findings.evidence: docs/briefs/B20261126-1036-b44-i98-self-update.loop-brief.md:305-308 says to run bare `go build` and then bare `vloop self-update`. The module root is the library package `vloop` (`embed.go:1-2`), so `go build` there does not produce the command binary; the command is `./cmd/vloop`. In this pwsh environment, `Get-Command vloop` resolves the installed GOBIN executable rather than a repository-local executable, so a later bare `vloop self-update` would test the installed release, not the branch build.
findings.fix: Name the main package and invoke its output explicitly, for example `go build -o .vloop/tmp/vloop.exe ./cmd/vloop` followed by `& ./.vloop/tmp/vloop.exe self-update`, or run `go run ./cmd/vloop self-update` for the refusal check.

findings.summary: The `--version` worked example omits lines the behaviour contract requires.
findings.evidence: docs/briefs/B20261126-1036-b44-i98-self-update.loop-brief.md:280-281 renders the v0.15.0-rc.5 case as `installing ... … … exit 0`. S1 step 7 requires the `installed vloop <target> at <dir>` line, and the text at lines 192-195 requires a `! with --version` warning before S2; the example shows neither, nor the resulting plugin and next lines.
findings.fix: Expand that case to the complete literal output in contract order: installing, installed, the `--version` warning, the Claude result, and the next-step line, with the exact exit 0.

findings.summary: The roadmap row the brief says its ready commit will add is still absent.
findings.evidence: docs/briefs/B20261126-1036-b44-i98-self-update.loop-brief.md:18-19 promises a B44 row in docs/design-notes/vloop-roadmap-b18-b21.md. That file currently ends its sequence at B41 (line 48); a search finds no B44 row.

decisions: Keep `vloop self-update` for machine-wide binary and plugin updates; `vloop upgrade` remains the per-repository operation. This separation is sound.
Use the Go toolchain and module proxy as the version and installation channel, not GitHub release APIs or assets. Sound and already followed by tools/release.
Without `--version`, install only a strictly newer semver target; allow an explicit target to install older or pre-release versions. Sound.
Refuse rather than guess for missing Go, checkout builds, or a running executable outside Go's install directory. Sound.
Keep doctor and `vloop upgrade` offline; only `self-update` performs release lookup and plugin updates. Sound.
Treat plugin failures as reportable but non-fatal after the binary step. Approved tradeoff; retain the pinned retry command.
Amend C-2 for paths outside a repository: slash-separated and home-shortened with `~`. Necessary for this command and explicitly scoped.

Fake Go and both agent CLIs with temporary Go programs, use golang.org/x/mod/semver, and let `--check --version` compare with the explicit target. These mechanics preserve the Windows and offline-test requirements.
checked: facts, consistency, rules, runnability; brief structure, dependencies, binding references, domain/platform invariants, config checks, build/module-version handling, doctor plugin discovery, release Go commands, agent update syntax, and the Windows executable move-aside assumption
